subsystem: World View (Earth globe, live layers, full God's Eye View engine, Ask Celine on the map)
summary: World View has two globes. Clicking Earth (or 'World View' in the Command header) opens /world, which is now only a shell that starts the full God's Eye View engine (a Node.js app pinned in integrations/gods-eye-view); it shows nothing until you have run Setup-Apex-World.cmd with Node 24.14+ or 26 installed, and it has never been tried on the laptop. The older 'basic globe' at /world/basic is the well-tested part: place search, satellite/street maps, and three live layers (earthquakes, regional aircraft, space stations) plus an Ask Celine box that goes through normal Apex chat. Its 3D globe library (Cesium) is fetched from a CDN, so neither globe works offline. The Ask Celine panel inside the full engine has a confirmed bug: its first step calls a map action ('get_scene_context') that the engine does not have, so every question should fail before reaching the model.

features.name: Earth portal on Command (entry point)
features.what: Clicking the Earth globe on the Command page, the 'Earth · World View' label, or the 'World View' link in the header opens World View in a full-screen dialog. Dragging the globe rotates it instead of opening it.
features.how_to_use: Command page (/) -> click Earth or the 'World View' header link. Escape or '<- Command' closes it. Home, Setup and Apps pages also link to /world.
features.evidence: dashboard/static/index.html:33 loads world-launch.js; index.html:161 and :199 have the links; dashboard/static/world-launch.js:37-77 builds the dialog with an iframe to /world; scripts/check_world_entry_ui.cjs and scripts/check_world_view_ui.cjs:131 check the iframe src. /world is in the no-auth shell list at dashboard/server.py:277.
features.setup_needed: None for the portal itself, but what opens inside it is the full engine (see next feature), which needs setup.

features.name: Full World View engine (God's Eye View) at /world
features.what: A pinned copy of the open-source God's Eye View app (26 layers, including satellites, flights, military flights, vessels, traffic, cameras, weather, fires, cables and launches, plus HUD/sensor styles, drawing and routes). Apex starts it on demand as a hidden Node process on a random local port and passes requests through an authenticated gateway.
features.how_to_use: Click Earth on Command, or open http://127.0.0.1:7860/world. It shows 'Opening the complete world engine...' and then loads the engine in a frame. If it fails, the page offers links to /world/basic and /setup.
features.evidence: dashboard/world.py:37-39 (/world serves world-engine.html; confirmed with TestClient: GET /world returns the engine shell, not the basic globe); dashboard/static/world-engine-shell.js:11-23 (session, then iframe to /world/engine/); dashboard/world_engine.py:85-127 (EngineRuntime.start: needs 'node' on PATH and node_modules/vite, 45 s health deadline, max 3 starts in 120 s); dashboard/world_engine.py:179-231 (gateway); dashboard/server.py:255-261 (auth for /world/engine/); integrations/gods-eye-view/apex-server.mjs:38 (rebuilds the whole production bundle before serving if dist/ is missing or the fingerprint changed). Tests: tests/test_world_engine.py (14 tests, all with the Node process faked; no test starts the real engine). Here: node_modules is absent and this machine has Node 22, which the engine refuses, so the real engine was never run in this environment.
features.setup_needed: Install Node.js 24.14+ (24.x) or 26.x, then run Setup-Apex-World.cmd once (it verifies 1551 pinned files, runs npm ci and a production build). Needs internet for npm and for most map layers. Rerun after any update that changes integrations/gods-eye-view.

features.name: Ask Celine inside the full engine
features.what: A toolbar button 'Ask Celine' in the full engine opens a panel where you type (or speak) a question; Apex's model is given the engine's 30 map actions (fly to, show layer, track entity, annotate, next ISS pass...) and the page runs them, with optional spoken replies through local Celine.
features.how_to_use: In /world, click 'Ask Celine' at the top, type a question and Send; tick 'Speak replies' for voice; 'Microphone' uses the browser's speech recognition.
features.evidence: integrations/gods-eye-view/apex-bridge.js:62 calls runner('get_scene_context', ...) before contacting Apex; the engine's action runner (integrations/gods-eye-view/src/voice/gevActions.js:346-1163) only handles named actions and ends with throw new Error('Unknown GEV tool: ' + name); 'get_scene_context' appears nowhere in the engine source or in APEX_ACTIONS.json (30 actions, closest is get_current_view_state). The throw is caught at apex-bridge.js:81 and printed, so the model is never asked. Server side (dashboard/world_assistant.py:50-135) is tested in tests/test_world_engine.py:120-174 with the browser faked; apex-bridge.js itself has no test.
features.setup_needed: Engine setup as above, plus an API key for the active model (DeepSeek for deepseek-flash). Needs a code fix first.

features.name: Basic globe at /world/basic
features.what: The original Apex globe: drag/zoom/tilt the Earth, switch between satellite imagery, street map or bare globe, click to mark a point, quick buttons for Byblos, Beirut and Rome. It remembers the camera and map in the browser.
features.how_to_use: Open http://127.0.0.1:7860/world/basic, or click 'Open the basic globe and existing saved projects' on the World View loading screen.
features.evidence: dashboard/world_engine.py:159-161 (/world/basic route); dashboard/static/world.html; dashboard/static/world-view.js:47-76 (loads Cesium 1.124 from cdn.jsdelivr.net, line 6, with a 20 s timeout); dashboard/static/world/imagery.js:7-10 (OpenStreetMap and Esri tiles). Page checks: scripts/check_world_view_ui.cjs. The real-browser check scripts/check_world_view_browser.cjs:83 is stale (see gaps).
features.setup_needed: Internet: the Cesium library and map tiles come from the web. Does not work offline.

features.name: Place search
features.what: Type a city, landmark or 'lat, lng' and fly there. Names are looked up on Photon (OpenStreetMap); coordinates are handled in the browser. Results are cached 10 minutes and searches are limited to one per second.
features.evidence: dashboard/world.py:69-104 (/api/world/search); dashboard/static/world-view.js:239-280; tests/test_world_view.py (5 tests: auth, validation, filtering, cache, provider failure).
features.setup_needed: Internet (photon.komoot.io). Signed in with the dashboard token in this browser.

features.name: Earthquakes layer (USGS)
features.what: Shows M2.5+ earthquakes from the past day as markers sized by magnitude, with magnitude, depth, times, review status and a USGS link. Refreshes each minute while visible and marks old data as stale.
features.how_to_use: /world/basic -> Live layers -> tick 'Earthquakes · M2.5+ · past day'. Or type 'show earthquakes' in Ask Celine.
features.evidence: dashboard/world_layers.py:85-106 (/api/world/layers/earthquakes, 60 s server cache, 2 MiB cap); dashboard/static/world-earthquakes.js:116; tests/test_world_layers.py (8 tests); scripts/check_world_earthquakes_ui.cjs.

features.name: Regional aircraft layer (ADSB.lol)
features.what: Shows aircraft reported within 250 nautical miles of the place you picked (default Byblos), with callsign, registration, type, altitude, speed and track. Refreshes every 30 seconds; older positions are dimmed.
features.how_to_use: /world/basic -> Live layers -> tick 'Aircraft · regional', pick a place, then 'Load this area'. Or say/type 'show flights'.
features.evidence: dashboard/world_flights.py:88-135 (/api/world/layers/flights, 30 s region cache, 16 regions, 429 back-off); dashboard/static/world-flights.js:117; tests/test_world_flights.py (9 tests); scripts/check_world_flights_ui.cjs.
features.setup_needed: Internet (api.adsb.lol). Coverage over Lebanon depends on volunteer receivers.

features.name: Space stations layer (CelesTrak + SGP4)
features.what: Downloads orbit data for the space-station group (ISS and others) at most every 2 hours, saves it next to Apex's database, and calculates positions in the browser every second, with the predicted next orbit for a selected station.
features.how_to_use: /world/basic -> Live layers -> tick 'Satellites · space stations'. 'Retry source' only works after the 2-hour cooldown.
features.evidence: dashboard/world_satellites.py:108-153 (/api/world/layers/satellites and /satellites/retry; cache file from longterm.DB_PATH, line 22-25); dashboard/static/world-satellites.js:13 loads the local satellite-6.0.2.min.js; tests/test_world_satellites.py (6 tests); scripts/check_world_satellites_ui.cjs.
features.setup_needed: Internet (celestrak.org) for the first download; positions then calculate locally from the saved file.

features.name: Ask Celine on the basic globe
features.what: A box where you ask about what is on the map. Simple commands ('show flights', 'hide satellites', 'show earthquakes', 'reset globe') run directly; other questions go to the normal Apex chat with a server-checked summary of your enabled layers and selected item. Answers can be spoken by local Celine.
features.how_to_use: /world/basic -> right panel -> 'Ask Celine' -> type and 'Ask Apex'; 'Microphone' uses browser speech recognition; tick 'Speak using local Celine'.
features.evidence: dashboard/static/world/live.js:114-130 (commands and /api/chat); dashboard/server.py:1565-1568 (adds scene_context); dashboard/world_live.py:127-156; tests/test_world_live.py (6 tests incl. test_chat_gets_server_selection_never_client_metadata); scripts/check_world_live_ui.cjs.
features.setup_needed: A working model key. Speech output needs the Celine/Voicebox server running; the mic needs a browser with speech recognition (Chrome/Edge, which sends audio to the vendor).

features.name: World projects on the basic globe (notes, routes, terrain, 3D buildings)
features.what: Save notes at a selected point, draw routes, undo, export/import the project as a JSON file; turn on terrain, and OSM 3D buildings if you paste a Cesium ion token (not saved).
features.evidence: dashboard/static/world.html:63-71; handlers in dashboard/static/world/live.js (world-add-note, world-route, world-project-export/import/undo, world-terrain, world-buildings). Only page checks (scripts/check_world_live_ui.cjs); no Python tests; 3D buildings need a Cesium ion account. Notes are not migrated into the full engine (docs/FULL_WORLD_VIEW.md:37).
features.setup_needed: Internet; a Cesium ion token for buildings.

features.name: World View setup on /setup (provider keys, engine status, update check)
features.what: The Setup page shows whether the engine is installed/running, lets the owner save map-provider keys into the engine's own store, shows model/voice/apps readiness, and has a 'Check God's Eye update' button that only compares the pinned revision with GitHub (never installs).
features.how_to_use: Open /setup (from Home, the World View toolbar, or the engine's error screen).
features.evidence: dashboard/world_setup.py:23-103 (/setup, /api/setup/access, /api/setup/status, /api/setup/world-update, owner-only via dashboard/apps.py:14-17); dashboard/static/setup.js:32,39 (keys saved through /world/engine/api/setup/keys, which needs the engine running); tests/test_world_setup.py (8 tests); scripts/check_setup_ui.cjs.
features.setup_needed: Engine installed for the provider-keys part; owner dashboard token.

features.name: Background world model (agent context)
features.what: Not the map: every 5 minutes Apex summarises goals and recent awareness events into a 'world state' that is added to Celine's prompt; readable at /api/world-state.
features.how_to_use: Automatic when awareness is on (default on); GET /api/world-state to read it.
features.evidence: agent/world_model.py; agent/awareness.py:341-372 and :579 (client wired); app/resident.py:224-232 builds the same monitor in resident mode; config.py:108 AWARENESS_ENABLED default True; dashboard/server.py:1459; tests/test_world_state_fresh.py (3 tests). Only skimmed for this audit.

gaps.issue: Ask Celine in the full World View cannot work: apex-bridge.js first calls runner('get_scene_context'), an action the engine does not have, so the runner throws 'Unknown GEV tool: get_scene_context' and the question never reaches the model.
gaps.evidence: integrations/gods-eye-view/apex-bridge.js:62; integrations/gods-eye-view/src/voice/gevActions.js:1163 (final throw); APEX_ACTIONS.json has 30 actions and none is get_scene_context
gaps.fix_hint: Use runner('get_current_view_state', {}) (an existing action) for the context, or build the context in the bridge from window.__godsEyeView; add a browser or jsdom test that runs apex-bridge.js against the real runner. Also drop get_scene_context from the SYSTEM prompt in dashboard/world_assistant.py:18.
gaps.how_confirmed: Grepped the whole engine (src, json, mjs) for 'get_scene_context': it appears only in apex-bridge.js (and in the Python SYSTEM prompt). Read runGevAction (gevActions.js:346-1163): every branch is name === '<action>' and it ends with throw. Followed window.__godsEyeView.voiceCommands (src/app/tools.js:178) -> sessionCommands.js:42 (controller or session) -> realtimeController.js:76 (this.runner = the raw runner). No wrapper adds the action. No test runs apex-bridge.js.

gaps.issue: Clicking Earth now always opens the full engine, which needs Node 24.14+/26 and Setup-Apex-World.cmd. Without it the owner gets an error screen, not a globe. The tested basic globe is only reachable through a small link on that screen or by typing /world/basic.
gaps.fix_hint: Have /world check runtime.status()['installed'] (and that node is on PATH) and fall back to /world/basic automatically, with a banner explaining how to set up the full engine.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran TestClient: GET /world returns the engine shell (contains world-engine-shell, not world-reset); GET /world/basic returns the basic globe. Read EngineRuntime.start: it raises 'World engine dependencies are missing. Run Setup-Apex-World.cmd.' when node or node_modules/vite is missing; the shell shows that as an error.

gaps.issue: The engine may rebuild its whole production bundle when it starts, but Apex allows only 45 seconds for start-up before killing it. A rebuild happens whenever apex-bridge.js or apex.config.mjs changed after setup (for example after a git update), or when GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY / CESIUM_ION_TOKEN in Apex's .env differ from what setup saw. On a slow laptop a Cesium build can exceed 45 s. If it does, the build is killed, the next open starts it again, and after 3 tries in 2 minutes World View refuses to start.
gaps.evidence: integrations/gods-eye-view/apex-server.mjs:14-17,38 (fingerprint, rebuild before preview); dashboard/world_engine.py:95-98,115-127 (3 starts per 120 s, 45 s deadline, then stop()); config.py:6 loads Apex .env into os.environ, which the engine inherits (world_engine.py:102)
gaps.fix_hint: Rebuild in Setup-Apex-World.cmd and the update flow, not at start-up; or have apex-server answer /apex-health with a 'building' state and let Python wait longer while building.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read both files. The rebuild is awaited before preview() starts, so /apex-health cannot answer during the build, and the Python loop stops the process after 45 s. Not confirmed: how long the build actually takes on the laptop (node_modules are not installed here).

gaps.issue: Neither globe works offline or on a poor connection. The basic globe loads Cesium (several MB) from cdn.jsdelivr.net with a 20-second total timeout, and map tiles come from OSM/Esri. Nothing uses the offline PMTiles world map on D:.
gaps.evidence: dashboard/static/world-view.js:6 (BASE = jsdelivr), :57 (20000 ms timeout), :62 (error message); dashboard/static/world/imagery.js:7-10; grep for 'pmtiles|offline' in dashboard/world*.py and static world files returned nothing
gaps.fix_hint: Serve Cesium from the engine's node_modules/cesium build (or vendor it under dashboard/static) and add an offline imagery option that points at the Apocalypse PMTiles map.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read world-view.js loadEngine(): the timer starts before the download and fail() rejects with 'Check your internet connection'. Grepped the World View files for pmtiles/offline: no matches.

gaps.issue: The only real-browser check of the basic globe opens /world and waits for #world-reset, but /world now serves the engine shell. The check would time out, so the basic globe's real Cesium rendering has no working browser check.
gaps.fix_hint: Point the check at /world/basic and add a separate engine smoke check once Node 24 is available in CI.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the script (it boots the real dashboard.server app) and confirmed with TestClient that GET /world has no 'world-reset' element. Did not run the script (it needs Playwright, Chromium and internet).

gaps.issue: Docs overclaim the basic globe. docs/WORLD_VIEW.md says there is a Follow button, a searchable entity list and typed commands 'follow selected' / 'stop following', and that 'the standalone page is /world'. None of the follow features exist in the code, and /world is now the full engine.
gaps.evidence: docs/WORLD_VIEW.md:5-12; dashboard/static/world/live.js:115-121 (only show/hide and reset globe); grep -i follow over the World View static files finds only a CSS note
gaps.fix_hint: Rewrite the top of WORLD_VIEW.md to describe what /world/basic actually does, and remove the follow commands or build them.
gaps.how_confirmed: Grepped dashboard/static/world*.js, world/*.js and world.html for 'follow' (case-insensitive). The only hit is world.html:54 'size follows magnitude'.

gaps.issue: No automated test covers scripts/setup_world_engine.py, apex-server.mjs, apex-build.mjs or apex-bridge.js. Every engine test fakes the Node process, so the real start-up, gateway proxying to Vite preview and the Ask Celine bridge have never run under test. The engine pins Node 24.14+/26, but this environment has Node 22.
gaps.evidence: tests/test_world_engine.py:112-118 (start failure faked); grep for setup_world_engine/apex-server/apex-bridge in tests/ found no engine test; node --version here = v22.23.4
gaps.fix_hint: Add a test that runs setup_world_engine.verify_source() (it passes: 1551 files) and a Node-gated smoke test that starts apex-server.mjs and requests /apex-health.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran python3 scripts/setup_world_engine.py --verify-only (passed: 'Verified 1551 original God's Eye View files'). Grepped tests/ for the engine scripts and found nothing beyond faked runtime tests. Ran the 8 world test files: 85 passed in 6.9 s.

gaps.issue: After any failed CelesTrak download (for example during a power or internet cut), the space-station layer stays paused for 2 hours, and 'Retry source' does nothing until then because the cooldown is saved before the request.
gaps.evidence: dashboard/world_satellites.py:112-118 (retry clears paused but next_attempt is still 2 h ahead), :137
gaps.fix_hint: Use a shorter cooldown (for example 5-10 minutes) after a network error, keeping 2 h after success.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read _load(): with retry=True it sets paused=False and then returns early when now < next_attempt. The UI text says 'Retry source after its cooldown', so this is by design, and tests/test_world_satellites.py covers it.

gaps.issue: World Ask Celine holds one global lock for the whole model call (up to 90 s), so a second World View window or a slow model blocks every other world question.
gaps.fix_hint: Release the lock around the model call and only hold it for the turn bookkeeping.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the code: asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.to_thread(_complete...), 90) runs inside 'async with _lock'.

gaps.issue: If the engine process dies and is restarted, the previous log file handle is not closed before start() opens a new one (a small handle leak on Windows).
gaps.fix_hint: Close self.log in start() when the previous process has exited.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the lines only; the impact is minor and was not reproduced.

needs_from_owner: Check whether Node.js is installed and which version: run 'node --version' in PowerShell. World View needs 24.14+ (24.x) or 26.x.

Run Setup-Apex-World.cmd once (it needs internet for npm), then click Earth on Command and report whether the full World View opens or shows an error. If it errors, send .mcp-runtime\world-engine.log.
Time how long the first open takes after Setup and after the next Apex update (the 45-second start-up limit).
Open http://127.0.0.1:7860/world/basic and confirm the globe loads on the Lebanese connection, then try Earthquakes, Aircraft (Byblos) and Space stations.
In the basic globe's Ask Celine, ask 'what earthquakes are on?' with Earthquakes on, to confirm the deepseek-flash model answers with the layer context.
Do not rely on the full engine's 'Ask Celine' button until it is fixed. It is expected to show 'Unknown GEV tool: get_scene_context'.

rating.why: The basic globe and its three live layers are solid and well tested, but the main Earth button now opens a heavy Node engine that has never run on the laptop, its Ask Celine is broken, and nothing works offline.
